# PROJECT_FILE_MAP — Complete File-by-File Reference

**Scope:** everything tracked/working in this repository (backend + frontend + config), generated by reading the code. Skips generated/dependency directories (`node_modules/`, `.venv-py311/`, `__pycache__/`, `.next/`, `.pytest_cache/`, `.ruff_cache/`).

**How to read the labels:** 🔵 core = central to the current product, touched frequently. 🟢 support = utility/plumbing that core depends on. 🟠 legacy/dormant = superseded code kept for tests or wire compatibility, described in Section 6.

> **Inference notes (things I characterized structurally, not line-by-line):** `app/api/chat_v2.py` (2,184 lines), `app/api/workspaces.py` (744), `app/api/documents_v2.py` (707), `app/retrieval/intent.py`, `app/db/legacy_models.py` (527) and the frontend login page were described from module docstrings, route/def inventories and targeted reads rather than a full read of every line. Migration titles 0010–0016 are one-line summaries from their filenames plus surrounding context. Anything else was read directly.
>
> The map reflects the current working tree — which, as of this pass, includes an in-progress uncommitted change: the `WorkspaceSwitcher` component was just deleted (`frontend/src/components/workspace-switcher.tsx`) and `sidebar.tsx`/`workspace.tsx` edited to remove it (see Section 6).

## 2. BACKEND — FOLDER BY FOLDER

### `backend/app/` — root modules

| File | Purpose | Key exports | Label |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main.py` | App factory. `lifespan` auto-runs `alembic upgrade head` on startup (non-test envs), seeds the demo workspace, and starts the periodic demo-guest cleanup loop. Registers CORS, request-ID middleware, rate limiting, exception handlers, workspace-switch middleware, and all routers. Exposes `/health`. | `create_app()`; lazy `app` via `__getattr__` (import-safe without env) | 🔵 core |
| `config.py` | Every environment variable, Pydantic `BaseSettings` with provider presets (Groq/OpenRouter/Gemini display names), validation (e.g. candidate ≥ final retrieval counts), and a cached `get_settings()`. ~504 lines; fields span DB, Supabase, LLM keys, embedding model/dim, chunking, retrieval tuning, reranker, demo flags, Sentry, CORS, JWKS/JWT. | `Settings`, `get_settings()` | 🔵 core |
| `errors.py` | Global exception handling: pure-ASGI `RequestContextMiddleware` (assigns `x-request-id`, echoes it on every response, tags Sentry scope), HTTP/422/500 handlers that return only an opaque detail + request_id — internals never reach the client. | `register_request_context`, `register_exception_handlers` | 🟢 support |
| `logging_config.py` | Loguru setup: stdlib interop handler, request-ID in every record, JSON serialization in production. | `configure_logging()` | 🟢 support |

### `backend/app/api/` — HTTP routers

| File | Purpose | Key endpoints / exports | Label |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspaces.py` | Workspace CRUD, membership, invitations, stats. Multi-tenant: every route uses `tenant_session` + role dependencies from `workspace_deps`. Contains the invitation accept flow backed by the DB function from migration 0010. | POST/GET `{/workspaces}`, GET/PATCH/DELETE `/{id}`, members list/update/remove, invitations create/list, `POST /invitations/{id}/accept` (second router `accept_router`), `GET /{id}/stats` | 🔵 core |
| `documents_v2.py` | Canonical document lifecycle: upload (validate → checksum → owner: inline ingest to READY / member: PENDING), list/detail, approve (OWNER → inline ingest → READY), reject (→ REJECTED), delete. Invalidation of the routing/knowledge caches on document changes. ~707 lines. | `upload_document`, `approve_document`, `reject_document`, `delete_document`, `list_documents`, `get_document` | 🔵 core |
| `chat_v2.py` | The chat surface. `POST /chat` = SSE streaming endpoint (typed events: `session`, `sources`, `token`, `citations`, `done`, `error`) with per-turn persistence; `POST /chat/grounded` = synchronous JSON variant for tests. Big intent dispatch layer (`_answer_metadata_question`, `_answer_greeting`, `_answer_identity_*`, `_answer_conversation_history`, refusals…) plus session management (`GET /sessions`, `GET /sessions/{id}/messages`, `DELETE`). 2,184 lines — the largest file in the repo. | `chat_stream`, `grounded_chat`, `list_sessions`, `list_messages`, `delete_session` | 🔵 core |
| `auth.py` | Identity endpoints. `GET /me` returns verified identity + workspace name/role from the `members` table (never from the JWT); `POST /auth/check-email` asks Supabase's admin API whether an email is registered (boolean only, rate-limited, fail-open) so the login form can distinguish "no account" from "wrong password". | `read_me`, `check_email` | 🔵 core |
| `demo.py` | `POST /demo/enter` — creates an ephemeral Supabase guest (`guest_<uuid>@demo.local`), removes the trigger-provisioned workspace, and inserts a MEMBER membership in the demo workspace; returns credentials for the frontend to sign in with. | `demo_enter` | 🟢 support (demo only) |
| `dependencies.py` | FastAPI dependencies. `get_generic_llm` builds the LLM provider (fallback chain when >1 key configured, else plain generic). **`require_role` is an explicitly-documented legacy no-op shim** with zero callers left. | `get_generic_llm`, `require_role` (dead) | 🟢 support |
| `workspace_deps.py` | Workspace authorization dependencies: resolves the caller's ACTIVE membership row per workspace (404 on none — no ID enumeration), enforces OWNER vs MEMBER from the `members` table. | `WorkspaceOwner`, `WorkspaceMemberAny`, `assert_workspace_role`, `require_workspace_role` | 🔵 core |
| `__init__.py` | Empty. | — | — |

### `backend/app/security/` — the trust boundary

| File | Purpose | Key exports | Label |
|---|---|---|---|
| `auth.py` | JWT verification + request `Principal`. Accepts Supabase JWKS (ES256/RS256) or the shared HS256 secret — algorithm confusion is blocked by choosing the key store *from the allowed algorithm*, never trusting the header alone. `workspace_id` from verified claims (or `members`-table fallback); role is deliberately **not** in the Principal. Handles workspace-switch override + clock-skew leeway + JWKS retry cooldowns. | `Principal`, `get_principal`, `CurrentPrincipal`, `decode_token`, `reset_jwks_cache` | 🔵 core |
| `workspace_switch.py` | `X-Workspace-ID` header → contextvar override for the current request; `get_principal` validates membership in the requested workspace (403 otherwise). | `workspace_switch_middleware`, `get_requested_workspace_id` | 🔵 core |
| `rls.py` | Row-level-security plumbing: `tenant_session()` sets JWT claims (`request.jwt.claims`) **and** drops to `app_tenant` (NOBYPASSRLS — Supabase's `postgres` role has BYPASSRLS and would ignore policies), all `LOCAL` to the transaction. | `tenant_session`, `set_tenant_claims`, `use_tenant_role` | 🔵 core |
| `uploads.py` | Upload validation before any extraction library sees a byte: streaming size cap (413), extension allowlist (pdf/docx/xlsx/csv/txt/md/markdown — 415), **content sniffing** of leading bytes (PDF magic, ZIP/OOXML, NUL-free UTF-8), filename sanitization (NFKC, traversal strip). Bytes stored under a generated UUID key. | `stream_to_storage`, `ALLOWED_TYPES`, `UploadRejected`, `resolve_type`, `verify_content_matches`, `safe_display_filename` | 🔵 core |
| `rate_limit.py` | SlowAPI wiring: per-token/IP key, `UPLOAD_RATE_LIMIT` (20/min) and `CHAT_RATE_LIMIT` (60/min). | `limiter`, `register_rate_limiting` | 🟢 support |
| `untrusted.py` | Defensive fencing for external text: wraps content in nonce-tagged `BEGIN/END_UNTRUSTED…` fences and rewrites anything fence-like. Used by the prompt layer's twin in `rag/prompts.py`. | `fence`, `neutralize` | 🟢 support (currently no MCP/tool sources, but the RAG prompt layer applies the same pattern) |

### `backend/app/retrieval/` — **LIVE retrieval intelligence** (the product's brain)

| File | Purpose | Key exports | Label |
|---|---|---|---|
| `intent.py` | Deterministic + LLM-assisted **intent classification**: enums (`IntentCategory`, `MetadataSubIntent`, `QueryShape`…), regex classification (`classify_intent_regex`) with hundreds of hand-tuned rules, an LLM route path, and per-category sub-intents (doc descriptions, company name, member metadata, conversation history). ~1,200+ lines. | `classify_intent`, `classify_intent_regex`, `normalize_for_classification`, `Intent`, `QueryShape`, `IntentCategory` | 🔵 core |
| `llm_router.py` | LLM-based router for ambiguous queries that the regex layer can't decide; returns a `RouteResult` (category + confidence) parsed from the model's JSON-ish answer. | `route_with_llm`, `RouteResult` | 🔵 core |
| `routing_cache.py` | In-memory per-workspace cache of intent classifications (LRU-capped), invalidated on document lifecycle events. | `get_cached_route`, `set_cached_route`, `invalidate_workspace_cache`, `get_cache_stats` | 🔵 core |
| `workspace_knowledge.py` | Per-workspace "knowledge file" (document names/types/descriptions + member info) injected into the LLM router prompt so it can route name-aware queries; cached + invalidated on changes. | `get_workspace_knowledge`, `invalidate_workspace_knowledge`, `WorkspaceKnowledge` | 🔵 core |
| `pipeline.py` | The orchestrator: `retrieve()` runs hybrid search → RRF fuse → rerank → grounding; dataclasses `RetrievedChunk`/`RetrievalResult` carry citations and the `had_evidence` flag. | `retrieve`, `RetrievedChunk`, `RetrievalResult` | 🔵 core |
| `hybrid.py` | Semantic (pgvector cosine) + keyword (tsvector) search over canonical chunks, RRF fusion (`1/(k+rank)`, k=60), plus a filename-token matcher so "what's in the devops doc?" finds the right file. | `semantic_search`, `keyword_search`, `rrf_merge`, `filename_search` | 🔵 core |
| `rerank.py` | Lazy-loaded local cross-encoder (`ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2`); scores query/chunk pairs on CPU. Never loads at import. | `get_reranker`, `rerank_scores`, `reset_reranker` | 🔵 core |
| `grounding.py` | Layer-1 retrieval grounding: threshold decision on the top rerank score (`is_grounded`) plus an overview-aggregate variant. | `is_grounded`, `is_overview_grounded` | 🔵 core |
| `relevance.py` | Pre-retrieval relevance gate: is the question on-topic for this workspace at all? Regex fast-path + optional LLM check, returns a `RelevanceDecision`. | `check_relevance`, `RelevanceDecision` | 🔵 core |
| `doc_targeting.py` | Detects "the <filename> document" references in a question and fuzzy-matches them against workspace document names, producing a targeting score used to relax retrieval thresholds. | `detect_document_reference`, `resolve_document_target`, `DocumentTargetingResult` | 🔵 core |
| `query_rewrite.py` | Conversation-context rewriting: detects pronoun/reference follow-ups needing the last turns, calls the LLM to produce a standalone query. | `rewrite_query`, `RewriteResult`, `ChatTurn` | 🔵 core |
| `refusals.py` | Central refusal policy — one `ResponseReason` enum, one message template per reason (NO_EVIDENCE, NOT_RELEVANT, OUT_OF_SCOPE, …). | `ResponseReason`, `refusal_message` | 🔵 core |
| `__init__.py` | Package docstring. | — | — |

### `backend/app/rag/` — **split package** (three live extractors + a legacy retrieval stack)

| File | Purpose | Key exports | Label |
|---|---|---|---|
| `extraction.py` | Text extraction from uploaded files: PDF (PyMuPDF, per-page), DOCX (python-docx, paragraphs + tables), XLSX, TXT, Markdown, CSV (pandas-style, headers repeated per page block). Includes zip-bomb/OOXML-kind guards, `normalize_text`, `count_words`, page-accurate `ExtractedPage` records. | `extract_pages`, `ExtractedPage`, `ExtractionError`, `normalize_text`, `count_words` | 🔵 core (ingestion depends on it) |
| `chunking.py` | Splits extracted pages into overlapping chunks via LangChain's `RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter` (config-pinned chunk size/overlap), preserving the locator (page/section) for citations. | `chunk_pages`, `Chunk` | 🔵 core |
| `embeddings.py` | Local sentence-transformers embeddings (`bge-small-en-v1.5`, 384-dim), lazy-loaded, batched, with `embed_passages_resilient` (positional `None` for chunks that fail — one bad chunk never kills a document) and retry logic. | `get_model`, `embed_passages_resilient`, `embed_query`, `reset_model` | 🔵 core |
| `prompts.py` | Prompt construction for RAG answers: `format_context` fences chunks with a nonce (untrusted-data defense), `build_messages` builds the strict "answer only from context" system prompt. | `build_messages`, `format_context` | 🔵 core (used by chat_v2) |
| `pipeline.py` | **Mostly superseded** pre-Phase-5 "RAG answer pipeline" (`retrieve_for_question`, `stream_answer`, `resolve_citations`, `source_payload`). Only `cited_numbers(answer)` is still imported by `chat_v2.py`. | `cited_numbers` (live) | 🟠 legacy (one helper live) |
| `retrieval.py` | **Fully legacy** vector retrieval over the *legacy org-centric* models (`app.db.legacy_models`). Only consumed by `rag/pipeline.py` above; no live route touches it. | `retrieve_chunks`, `build_context` | 🟠 legacy (dead chain) |

### `backend/alembic/` — schema history (16 migrations)

`env.py` targets **only** the canonical `Base.metadata` from `app/db/base.py` (legacy metadata is deliberately invisible to autogenerate).

| Migration | What it does |
|---|---|
| `0001_initial_schema` | Org-centric start: orgs, users, documents, chunks, chat, RLS |
| `0002_tenant_role_set` | Let the app role drop into `app_tenant` so RLS applies |
| `0003_sql_agent_role_audit` | SQL-agent read-only role + query audit log (era now removed) |
| `0004_auth_provisioning` | Every Supabase signup auto-provisions an org + users row + claims |
| `0005_ingestion_hardening` | Ingestion progress columns + dead-letter table (era now removed) |
| `0006_workspaces` | First `workspaces`/`workspace_members`/conversation-summary tables |
| `0007_document_visibility` | Org-wide vs personal document visibility |
| `0008_phase1c_canonical_schema` | **The pivot:** replaces the org-centric schema with the canonical multi-tenant workspace schema (documents BYTEA-ready, `members`, workspace-scoped RLS policies incl. `document_chunks_write`) |
| `0009_phase1c_finalize_bytes` | Enforce `file_data`/`checksum` NOT NULL, drop `storage_key` |
| `0010_phase2_accept_invitation` | DB-side invitation acceptance (raises typed SQLSTATEs the API maps to HTTP) |
| `0011_add_document_description` | Adds `documents.description` |
| `0012_org_creation_limit` | Caps orgs a user can create (frontend says max 4) |
| `0013_one_org_per_email` | One org per email constraint |
| `0014_workspace_verification` | Workspace verification hardening |
| `0015_revert_to_one_org_per_email` | Reverts/redoes the one-org-per-email approach (final behavior: auto-provisioned org per signup is deleted/replaced by membership in the demo workspace for guests) |
| `0016_add_workspace_delete_policy` | RLS policy enabling workspace deletion |

*(0010–0016 summarized from filenames + code references; 0001–0009 titles read from their docstrings.)*

## 3. BACKEND — TESTS

### `backend/tests/conftest.py` + shared fixtures
- `conftest.py` (root): global fixtures — env isolation/`valid_env` behavior, `.env` ignoring where noted in sub-suites.
- `unit/conftest.py`: standardized fakes — fake SQLAlchemy sessions/results, a "smart mock" LLM router (single source of routing truth), and the `StubLLM` provider used across unit tests. **Central to understanding the whole unit suite.**

### `backend/tests/unit/` (38 files)
| File | Actually covers |
|---|---|
| `test_models.py` | Canonical §7 schema via ORM metadata inspection (no DB): table/columns/constraints, and that `legacy_models` stays isolated on its own metadata |
| `test_db_session.py` | Engine/session wiring without a live DB |
| `test_config.py` | §13 env config loads/validates/never leaks secrets; LLM key overrides |
| `test_errors.py` | Global error handler never leaks internals (500 body has no secret markers) |
| `test_chunking.py` | Chunking preserves the locator (page/section) that citations are built from |
| `test_extraction.py` | Extractors return text + accurate locators and refuse hostile files (zip bombs, wrong-kind OOXML) |
| `test_normalization.py` | Text normalization before embedding (invisible chars, whitespace runs) |
| `test_embedding_resilience.py` | `embed_passages_resilient` positional-None semantics — one bad chunk ≠ lost document |
| `test_fallback.py` / `test_fallback_chain.py` | Fallback chain with mocked httpx: exact provider order, 429→next provider, context preserved across failover |
| `test_retrieval_hybrid.py` | Semantic + keyword + RRF fusion query *shape* (workspace scoping, limits) and fusion math on a fake session |

### `frontend/src/proxy.ts`
Route protection (Next 16 renamed `middleware.ts` → `proxy.ts`): redirects signed-out visitors off protected paths and signed-in visitors away from `/login` & co. Deliberately optimistic — the real boundary is the bearer token + RLS on every API call. Uses `getUser()` (validated) not `getSession()`, and writes refreshed cookies back onto the response.

## 6. ORPHANED, LEGACY & UNUSED FILES

**Clearly legacy / dead-end code (kept importable, no live route uses them):**
1. **`backend/app/rag/retrieval.py`** — legacy vector retrieval over `app.db.legacy_models` (org-centric). Only consumer is `rag/pipeline.py`. No live caller. 🔴
2. **`backend/app/rag/pipeline.py`** — the pre-Phase-5 RAG answer pipeline (`retrieve_for_question`, `stream_answer`, `resolve_citations`, `source_payload`). Superseded by `app/retrieval/pipeline.py` + `chat_v2.py`. **One exception:** `cited_numbers()` (imported twice by `chat_v2.py`) is still live, which is the only reason this file survives. ⚠️ borderline — could move `cited_numbers` out and delete.
3. **`backend/app/db/legacy_models.py`** — full org-centric model set on `LegacyBase`. Deliberately retained because the legacy tests in #4 (and the rag chain above) import from it; docstring says it is scheduled for deletion once its consumers are rebuilt. Not dead *by design*, but zero production code imports it.
4. **`backend/app/api/dependencies.py: require_role`** — self-documented "legacy compatibility shim… kept so legacy routers continue to compile", but there are **no legacy routers left**, so it has no callers at all. Candidate for deletion.
5. **`backend/scripts/run_acceptance.py` / `run_acceptance2.py` / `run_acceptance3.py`** — three near-duplicate one-off live-acceptance scripts (same 15 queries; variants add delays / diagnostics). Dev-only, not referenced by app or tests. Candidate to consolidate to one or archive.
6. **`backend/scripts/backfill_file_data.py`** — one-time byte backfill, already executed per Phase 1C history; kept as a record.

**Legacy *wire/UI* remnants in the frontend (dormant, not dead code — the types/UI still exist but the backend never feeds them):**
7. **`RoutingEvent`/`StepEvent`/`AgentRoute`/`sql_query` in `frontend/src/lib/api/types.ts`, `parseEventStream`'s `KNOWN_EVENTS`, the `routing`/`step`/`sql_query` handling in `use-chat.ts`, `RoutingIndicator`, and `SqlDisclosure`.** The current backend SSE emits only `session`, `sources`, `token`, `citations`, `done`, `error` — no `routing` or `step` frames, and every `done` frame carries `routes: []` / `sql_query: ""` purely for backward compatibility. So `RoutingIndicator` and `SqlDisclosure` render nothing today, `turn.routes`/`turn.steps`/`turn.sqlQuery` stay empty, and the `AgentRoute` values (`business_data`, `external`, `direct`) describe the removed supervisor/SQL-agent architecture. Flagged here so nobody "fixes" them into working again by accident.
8. **`frontend/src/components/visibility-badge.tsx`** — no imports anywhere in `src` (verified by search). Orphaned component (the org-vs-personal visibility concept it displayed was removed with the org-centric document model).
9. **Document-scope remnants:** `DocumentVisibility = "org" | "personal"` type and `DocumentScope` in `api/types.ts` are "kept for UI compatibility" per their own comments — the current backend has no visibility field on `DocumentSummary`.

**Already removed this session:** `frontend/src/components/workspace-switcher.tsx` (deleted; the Workspace dropdown UI at the top of the sidebar) — `sidebar.tsx` and `workspace.tsx` were edited to drop its JSX and the now-dead `onSwitchWorkspace` wiring. Underlying `workspace_id` resolution (`activeWorkspaceId ?? me?.workspace_id` + `X-Workspace-ID`) is untouched.

**Non-app artifacts (not tracked / agent-local):** `.claude/` (local settings + worktrees), `Claude-NVIDIA-Setup/` (stray nested folder of unknown tooling provenance, gitignored), `memory/fix-seed-rls-claims.json` (committed agent session-memory note about the seed/RLS fix), and repo-root `.env` (present on this machine, gitignored).

**Naming drift worth knowing:** the Python package/project is still named `enterprise-ai-agent-backend` and several frontend docstrings reference "agents"/"supervisor"/"SQL" — all leftovers from an earlier multi-agent + SQL-agent architecture that this project deliberately dropped (CLAUDE.md §11). The current product is a single-pipeline document RAG assistant. Reading old comments without this context is misleading; the code (routers in `main.py`, `retrieval/` package) is the source of truth.
